chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Mahbub from Ibn Ri'ab from Hamzah ibn Humran, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And remember your Lord if you forget.' He said: 'That is regarding the oath. When you say: 'By Allah, I will do such and such,' and then you remember that you did not make a condition (of Allah's will), then say: 'If Allah wills.'
ai.seo_question: How to correct an oath made without saying 'if Allah wills' according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the command to 'remember your Lord if you forget' specifically applies to the omission of *insha'Allah* (if Allah wills) when making oaths. This establishes a practical mechanism for rectifying unilateral oaths by verbally invoking divine will upon remembrance, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on maintaining the flexibility of human agency under God's ultimate decree.
